---
title: "Building and testing"
---

This page will help you get started developing on ToFScope. All commands should be run from the repository root.
Python dependencies are managed with [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/); [Node](https://nodejs.org/en) is needed
to develop or rebuild the frontend. For more details on how the application is designed, see
[ToFScope architecture](30-architecture.qmd) for an overview of the application's architecture and its build.

## Install the development version of the Python package

```sh
git clone https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope.git
cd ToFScope
uv sync --frozen
```

## Install frontend dependencies

Install the exact versions in `frontend/package-lock.json` before working on the React and TypeScript interface:

```sh
npm --prefix frontend ci
```

This installs the frontend tools and dependencies into `frontend/node_modules/`. You will need to run it again
if the lockfile changes.

## Update the frontend API types

When the Python API changes, regenerate its OpenAPI schema and the TypeScript types used by the frontend:

```sh
npm --prefix frontend run generate:api
```

This updates `frontend/openapi.json` and `frontend/src/api/generated.ts`. Review and commit the generated changes with
the API change. The command uses the Python environment created by `uv sync` above.

## Check and test the frontend

```sh
npm --prefix frontend run typecheck
npm --prefix frontend test
```

The first command checks TypeScript without producing files; the second runs the Vitest frontend tests.

For browser workflows, run the Playwright suite:

```sh
npm --prefix frontend run test:e2e
```

These tests use Google Chrome and start local frontend and test backend servers by default. Install Chrome if it is not
already available; the CI setup uses `npm --prefix frontend exec -- playwright install --with-deps chrome` on Linux.

## Build the packaged frontend

The frontend application is bundled into the Python package, so users only need to install from PyPI and run `tofscope`
to start the app. On the developer side, this requires rebuilding the frontend assets into the Python package
and committing these files:

```sh
uv run python scripts/build_frontend.py
```

This script runs the frontend TypeScript and Vite build, replaces the generated files in `src/tofscope/static/`, and writes an
asset manifest. Rebuild after changing frontend sources so the Python package includes up-to-date browser assets.
During development, you will need to run this script to update what you see in the browser when testing manually.

## Test the Python application

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

This discovers and runs the Python test suite, including scientific calculations, storage, the API, and service behavior.

## Build and check distributions

After building the frontend assets, create the wheel and source distribution using `uv`. This example uses a
temporary directory to ensure a fresh context separate from the source directory:

```sh
artifact_dir=$(mktemp -d)
uv build --out-dir "$artifact_dir"
```

The wheel and source distribution both include the prebuilt browser assets. A source build will fail if those assets are
missing or stale. In the same terminal, install each artifact in a temporary environment and exercise the packaged
service and browser without Node:

```sh
uv run python scripts/check_distribution.py --artifacts "$artifact_dir" --output /tmp/tofscope-distribution
```

The script checks each artifact's version against the checkout, installs it in a temporary Python environment, and
creates disposable test acquisitions. It starts the installed service and uses Chrome to exercise preparation, plots,
identification, calibration, saving, reopening, and exports. It also checks that the packaged app runs without Node and
that the browser makes no unexpected external requests. These are smoke tests, not a replacement for the full test suites.
The goal of the script is to build ToFScope as a user would install it, then test both package formats in clean environments,
catching packaging problems that ordinary tests run from the source checkout might miss.

The temporary installations and test data are removed afterward. Results in `distribution.json` and screenshots are
written to the specified output directory; use a disposable location.

## Prepare a release

The repository includes a [`tofscope-release` agent skill](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/blob/main/.agents/skills/tofscope-release/SKILL.md)
for preparing and publishing releases. Ask a compatible coding agent to use the skill when preparing a ToFScope release.
It updates the version and generated assets, writes release notes, runs the relevant checks, and opens a draft pull request.

The agent waits for release approval at the draft pull request. Once approved, it completes the merge, tags the merged
commit to trigger PyPI publishing, creates the GitHub Release from the prepared notes, and starts a documentation rebuild
so the changelog includes the release. A tag triggers publication; it does not by itself confirm that publishing succeeded.

## Check the container

Container deployment is in early stages, but the `check_container.py` script will build a local Docker image and
run a non-root smoke test with read-only acquisition files and writable temporary
storage. It requires Docker and uses disposable test data:

```sh
uv run python scripts/check_container.py
```

The repository's CI workflow runs these checks and verifies that regenerated API files have no unexpected changes.

See [Maintaining the documentation](42-documentation.qmd) for information on building and previewing the documentation
site.
